candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive Alcian-Blue positive mucin, which are features of granuloma annulare. While necrobiotic xanthogranuloma also involves necrobiosis, the clinical presentation (painless induration below the eyelid, no mention of xanthomas or paraproteinemia) and the specific histopathological findings (extensive mucin) are more consistent with granuloma annulare. Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma typically presents with yellow-orange plaques/nodules and is often associated with paraproteinemia, neither of which is mentioned.
